t: The German Empire was formed by the unification of previously independent German states, under the rule of Kaiser Wilhelm I.
José Paranhos, Viscount of Rio Branco, began a four-year premiership as Prime Minister of the Empire of Brazil, the longest in the state's history.
William Woods Holden, Governor of North Carolina, became the first U.S. state governor to be removed from office through impeachment.
The Duke of Buckingham opened the first section of the Brill Tramway, a short railway line to transport goods between his lands and the national rail network.
Creatures of Impulse, by W. S. Gilbert, premiered at the Court Theatre in London.
The boiler of the Staten Island Ferry Westfield II exploded at South Ferry in New York City, killing at least 45 people.
The Great Chicago Fire, began and proceeded to destroy much of the city's central business district, killing 300 people and leaving 90,000 others homeless.
Liberian president Edward James Roye was overthrown in modern Africa's first coup d'état.
Sixteen-year-old Ella Stewart sent the first telegraphed message from Arizona Territory.
Aida, one of Giuseppe Verdi's most popular operas, made its debut in Cairo, Egypt.
Thespis, the first comic opera by Gilbert and Sullivan, premiered at the Gaiety Theatre in London.
